content:
claire: noticing a spike in streaming tail latency starting ~08:02 UTC, lots of SSE clients reporting long pauses. p95 for generation unchanged but p99 jumps to ~2.3s and some clients see complete stalls >10s. opening thread for triage and handoff
raj: oncall here, paging now. any customer impact flagged?
sarah: Support: two customers reported degraded UX (chat UI shows hang) and one flagged as P2. no data exfil or 5xxs from API frontends yet.
miguel: checking runtime. are these coming from a particular model or any streaming route?
claire: seems concentrated on /v1/chat/stream across hosted region eu-west-1. model=redwood-7b-quant, but also a few hits on gpt-adapter. starts at 08:02:12 UTC replicated across multiple pods.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-1999 - Streaming chunking stalls in eu-west-1. Severity: SEV2. Notifying eng-sre and eng-runtime.
raj: timeline notes: p95 ~320ms, p99 ~2300ms, tail beyond that for some traces. We saw proxy retries and backpressure metrics climb.
miguel: pulling proxy logs from edge-gw (envoy) — seeing continuous `upstream flush timed out` and `connection buffer full` messages. suspect buffering at the envoy->frontend-proxy hop.
claire: adding logs snippet:```
[08:02:14] envoy upstream write error: stream reset by peer, code=0x1e
[08:02:14] http2: stream 0 stalled, write buffer 65536/65536
[08:02:15] proxy retry for client x.x.x.x, attempt=1
```
raj: also seeing a surge in `client_window_exceeded` on websocket metrics — indicates client backpressure or slow reader. Could be a sudden influx of slow clients.
sarah: Customer note: "widgets freeze, then resume with burst text" — matches chunking + stall behavior.
miguel: quick checks: node-level CPU/GPU look normal; kernel tcp buffers fine. This smells like a transport-layer buffer saturation in envoy combined with some slow-consumer pattern from a new analytics client.
claire: mitigation plan: 1) enable immediate graceful degrade route to non-streaming (polling) for affected orgs, 2) bump envoy downstream write timeout to 30s temporarily, 3) identify offending clients and rate-limit. Who can push the route change?
raj: I can apply a canary route to redirect traffic for the flagged customer orgs to non-streaming endpoint. pinging deploy-bot to run the config change.
deploy-bot: @raj requested route update: applying canary redirect for org ids [org-8421, org-1992] now. Will confirm once in effect.
ops-bot: Reminder: include runbook link -> https://runbooks.internal/streaming-backpressure.
claire: while route redirect goes, miguel please tail the envoy upstream queue sizes and `proxy_downstream_write` metrics. also collect `sse_chunk_interval` histograms from the runtime.
miguel: on it. tail logs show queue_depth rising from 0 to ~400 per proxy instance right at spike. once we applied route redirect queue_depth drops to ~20 for the canaried nodes.
raj: canary redirect looks promising — support reports customer UI resumed for one org. p99 dropped from 2.3s to 480ms on canary.
sarah: I've informed the affected customer contacts with a short status update and told them we're mitigating; asked them for any recent client-side changes.
claire: next: find root cause — possible culprits: a) client-side slow readers, b) change in envoy version that reduced available write buffer, c) misconfigured keepalive/window sizing with new analytics agent. Check recent deploys around 07:50-08:00 UTC.
miguel: checking deploy history... there was an envoy config push to edge-gw cluster at 07:58 UTC that changed `http2_max_concurrent_streams` from 100 to 50.
raj: that fits: fewer concurrent streams => more head-of-line risk when slow readers occupy streams._rollout status?
deploy-bot: Envoy config change (cfg-ev-2026) applied to 60% of nodes at 07:58:21 UTC. Rollback not yet executed.
claire: decision: rollback cfg-ev-2026 immediately on remaining nodes and revert the 60% to prior config. miguel, can you coordinate rollback?
miguel: starting rollback to previous http2 concurrency and restoring buffer settings. will take ~4 mins to propagate.
raj: meanwhile, add temporary per-connection write window throttles: limit payload chunk size to 2KB and insert 50ms spacing between chunks for suspect clients as a stopgap.
claire: agree. also enable extra logging for identifying slow-consumer IPs and org ids.
ops-bot: Action items assigned: miguel (rollback + metrics), raj (canary redirect + throttles), sarah (customer comms), claire (postmortem owner).
miguel: rollback completed at 08:08 UTC, queue_depth on effected instances normalized. p99 now ~410ms cluster-wide, streaming stalls no longer reported.
raj: can we leave canary redirect in place for 30m and then remove once we validate stability?
claire: yes keep canary for 30m. collect traces and correlate with deploys to confirm root cause.
sarah: updated customers: mitigation applied, monitoring in place, we'll send a follow-up once we have an RCA.
claire: preliminary RCA hypothesis: envoy config change reduced HTTP/2 concurrency which increased head-of-line blocking when some clients became slow consumers; combined with tiny chunk sizes from the runtime caused more writes and buffer pressure, triggering upstream flush timeouts. Immediate fix: rollback config and introduce short-term throttles and canary redirect. Longer term: add adaptive backpressure detection and auto-fallback to polling, and add a pre-deploy checklist for http2 tuning.
raj: handoff to night oncall @ 08:11 UTC: leave canary and throttles, watch p99 and queue_depth. oncall: @miguel-night will take over.
miguel: acknowledged handoff. will keep monitoring for 2 hours and collect logs/tracesets for postmortem.
claire: thanks team. postmortem owner: claire. please add timeline and logs to INC-1999 and mark SEV2 resolved for now. :thumbsup:
